title: Post-deploy verification suite for VPC private deployments (Terraform outputs -> runtime readiness)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Deliver an automated post-deploy verification suite that runs immediately after Terraform completes a Private (VPC) deployment. The suite validates API readiness, model load correctness, and end-to-end inference smoke checks against the newly provisioned runtime.

Background: Private deployments are provisioned via Terraform modules that emit runtime endpoints and credentials. Historically we rely on manual validation or an ad-hoc sanity script. This causes delayed rollbacks and intermittent customer impact when upgrades or tainted resources leave a partially-initialized runtime. We need a robust, idempotent automation step that can be wired into apply-time or as a post-apply CI job to provide deterministic yes/no for promotion or rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Automated job runs automatically after terraform apply (or as a gated GH Actions workflow) and reports pass/fail to the deployment pipeline.
API readiness check: /ready and /health endpoints return 200 and JSON liveness keys within 30s endpoint availability window.
Model load validation: at least one reference model variant (small test model or quantized stub) loads successfully and reports stable KV cache readiness within 90s.
Smoke inference: 3 synthetic prompts across text-generation, chat, and structured-output paths succeed with expected response shape and latency < 600ms p50 for small models.
Failure modes return actionable diagnostics (logs bundle link, runtime pod/journalctl snapshots, and a single-line failure reason).
Results are visible in the deployment run with links to Redwood Console traces and a GitHub check annotation for CI gating.
steps: Consume Terraform outputs: runtime_endpoint, admin_token_secret_arn, model_bundle_uri from outputs.tf
API readiness probe: GET {runtime_endpoint}/health and GET {runtime_endpoint}/ready with Authorization: Bearer <admin_token>. Validate status 200 and required JSON keys: 'uptime', 'models_loaded'
Runtime introspection: call admin API to list loaded models and their state; if model not loaded, issue model-loading command via admin API and wait up to 90s with exponential backoff.

Model load smoke: trigger a small inference against the loaded test model (prompt set included in repo). Validate structure and tokenization sanity checks (no malformed JSON, required fields present).
Load/latency sample: run a 30-second, low-rps load test (3 concurrent connections) measuring p50/p95 latency and error rate. Fail if error_rate > 1% or p95 > 1200ms for the tiny test model.
Collect artifacts: runtime logs, kernel selection traces, kv-cache occupancy, and attach to the deployment job on success/failure.
Emit structured result: JSON summary to stdout and to deployment metadata store (Console run metadata) with keys: status, reason, metrics_url, logs_url.
For CI gating: mark the GitHub check as failure on overall suite failure and include actionable remediation hints.
runbook: If API /ready fails: fetch runtime system journal and last 200 lines of runtime.log, check for startup exceptions (OOM, CUDA driver mismatch).
If model fails to load: verify model artifact URI is accessible in the customer VPC; check S3/GCS IAM permissions and KMS decrypt success logs.
If smoke inference returns malformed output: capture request/response pair and raytracer logs; escalate to Serving Runtime on-call with annotated sample.

If p95 latency > threshold: scale up dedicated pool or mark deployment as degraded and trigger autoscaling policy for Dedicated; for Private, recommend operator step to increase node count or reduce batch size.

notes: Implementation must avoid using customer model weights in tests for privacy. Use a lightweight synthetic model bundle (quantized tiny) included in the infra repo. Keep secret material out of logs; use temporary signed URLs for artifact fetches and redact tokens. Coordinate with Security for the GH Action runner credentials to ensure least privilege.
suggested_rollback: On suite failure during a rolling upgrade: automatically stop rollout, revert to previous revision (if using canary) or re-run terraform apply with previous module tag. For full provision failures, mark the deployment as failed, notify the operator channel, and run automated cleanup of partially-created resources per infra cleanup playbook.
